question: Does an independent 240 ms owner authority deadline limit harmful movement overshoot when a pixel-derived task-relative guard loop is deterministically stalled for 340 ms?
task: rendered X11 tracker derived from existing container fixture with exogenous drift disabled to isolate authority during the injected guard-loop stall; controller uses pixels only; exact app state is scorer-only and read after controller exits

arms.GUARD_ONLY: same visual guard with loose 1000 ms owner cap, so the 340 ms controller stall delays guard cancellation
arms.DUAL_LIFETIME: same visual guard plus independent 240 ms owner deadline

hard_gates: terminal empty and balanced app-side key events in every arm
owner release verified in every arm
dual release occurs before stall end in every pair
guard-only release does not occur before stall end
primary_metric: independent harmful overshoot time while input is held, defined as exact scorer x < -0.02
PASS: all hard gates pass and DUAL_LIFETIME harmful overshoot is strictly lower than GUARD_ONLY in all 5 pairs
HOLD_OR_REJECT_NONUNIFORM: hard gates pass but overshoot advantage is not uniform
claim_scope: synthetic rendered-X11 fault-injection transfer only; not DOOM, model, human reaction or production safety
construction_history: smoke-0 failed before formal measurement because inherited exogenous drift moved initial x outside the intended source window before controller capture; repair disables drift rather than widening source tolerance

smoke-1 reached owner interruption but failed writing stop.flag because the arm output directory had not been created; repair creates the output directory at controller start and changes no scientific condition
